ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Ophthalmology (cataract) Referral — Jim Bridger

code.originalText: Establishing primary care for two years of blurred vision in both eyes with glare: vision, falls, driving, chronic low back pain at an old arrow-wound site, a goiter, sore knees, mood, and an ophthalmology consultation

text.paragraph: Two years of gradual, painless blurring of vision in both eyes, worse on the right, with glare and trouble recognizing faces, in a 70-year-old retired backcountry guide who has had one fall at dusk and has stopped driving at night. Please establish the cause, exclude glaucoma, macular degeneration and diabetic eye disease, and advise on surgery. [S]
Urgency: Routine, within two to three weeks. [S]

list.item: What is the cause of the vision loss, and are glaucoma, macular degeneration and diabetic retinopathy excluded?
Is surgery indicated, and on which eye first?
What lens implant and timing do you advise for the two eyes, and is same-day surgery on both eyes an option?
What drops and postoperative visits will he need, and how can he manage them without reading?
What should we advise about falls and driving before, between and after the operations?

text.paragraph: Gradual blurring in both eyes over about two years, right worse than left, with glare from sunlight and headlights, faded colors and difficulty recognizing faces across a room; no flashes, floaters, pain, redness or double vision. One fall on the porch steps at dusk in the past year without injury; stopped driving at night six months ago. He does not read, so reading vision is not a useful measure; he relies on his eyes for his orchard, his truck and his horse. No diabetes (HbA1c 5.5% today), no steroid use, no eye injury or surgery. Chronic low back pain at an old arrow-wound site, a long-standing multinodular goiter (TSH 1.62, free T4 1.2) and knee osteoarthritis treated with diclofenac gel; no other medicines; no known allergy; never smoked. Examination today: Snellen acuity 20/200 right and 20/100 left with his old glasses, no better with pinhole; pupils equal and reactive without an afferent defect; red reflex dull on the right; blood pressure 138/78. Please explain findings and plans to him aloud; written material should be read to him [S]

list.item: He can no longer see faces, the ground at dusk or the road at night, and is afraid of losing his sight altogether. [S]
An old ache in his lower back where the arrow went in, and sore knees on the orchard slopes. [S]
He wants to keep working his orchard, riding and driving into town. [S]

text.paragraph: Historical basis. These claims are historical evidence, not findings from a modern examination.

list.item: James Bridger was born on March 17, 1804, in Richmond, Virginia, the son of James and Chloe Bridger. The family moved west to Missouri when he was a boy, and his mother, a brother and his father died there within a few years, leaving him an orphan at about fourteen with a younger sister. [D]

After an apprenticeship as a blacksmith, he joined William Ashley's fur-trapping expedition to the Rocky Mountains in 1822. He spent more than four decades in the West as a trapper, a partner in a fur company, a trader, and from 1849 to 1868 a guide and scout for emigrants, surveyors and the Army. [D]
In a fight with Blackfeet men in 1832 he was struck in the back by two arrows; the iron head of one could not be removed and stayed deep in his back. [D]

In August 1835, at the fur traders' rendezvous on the Green River, the missionary physician Marcus Whitman removed the arrowhead from his back. A companion of Whitman's described an iron arrowhead three inches long, hooked at the point where it had struck a large bone and surrounded by tissue that had grown around it; the operation was difficult, and Bridger bore it steadily while trappers and Indians watched. [D]
In 1843 he and his partner Louis Vasquez founded Fort Bridger, a trading post for emigrants on Blacks Fork of the Green River in what is now southwestern Wyoming. [D]

He married three Native women in succession: the daughter of a Flathead chief, who died in 1846; a Ute woman, who died in 1849; and in 1850 a Shoshone woman. He had several children, some of whom he sent to school in Missouri. [D]
He could not read, but he enjoyed having books read aloud to him; an army officer's account from his scouting years describes him listening to Shakespeare's plays read until midnight. [D]

By his early sixties the effects of arthritis, rheumatism and rugged frontier life had caught up with him; in 1867 at Fort Phil Kearny he was troubled by rheumatism that hampered his movements, and in 1868 he moved back to his farm near Westport, Missouri. [D]
In his later years he had a goiter and a rupture (hernia), which troubled him somewhat; the cause of the goiter is not recorded. [D]

His eyesight began to fail in the late 1860s, and from 1873 it failed rapidly, so that he could recognize friends only by the sound of their voices. The cause of his failing sight is not recorded in the sources read. [D]

list.item: Gradual, painless blurring of vision in both eyes over about two years, worse in the right, with glare from sunlight and oncoming headlights, faded colors, and trouble recognizing faces across a room; Snellen acuity 20/200 right and 20/100 left with his old glasses, no better with a pinhole; no flashes, floaters, pain or redness; cause under evaluation with an ophthalmology consultation: active, confirmed [S]

Chronic low back pain for many years, aching across the lower back and worst on the side of an old arrow-wound scar over the right lower back, stiff in the morning and after long rides in his truck; no leg pain, numbness, weakness, bladder or bowel change, fever or weight loss; no red flags: active, confirmed [S]

Nontoxic multinodular goiter, present for decades: a firm, nodular, non-tender thyroid enlargement with no pressure symptoms (no trouble swallowing or breathing, no voice change); euthyroid: active, confirmed [S]
Primary osteoarthritis of both knees, aching on stairs and after walking the orchard, with morning stiffness under half an hour, crepitus and bony enlargement: active, confirmed [S]
One fall in the past year, missing the bottom step of the porch at dusk, without injury; poor vision in low light and contrast; at risk of further falls: active, confirmed [S]

Vision work-up at intake: visual acuity with and without pinhole, pupils, red reflex and a functional history (faces, reading signs, driving, glare, falls); HbA1c for diabetic retinopathy risk; urgent eye care for any sudden loss, pain or redness. Guideline: Cataract in the Adult Eye Preferred Practice Pattern (2021); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, cataract and rheumatoid arthritis/osteoarthritis monographs (2026) [S]

Falls and low vision: brighter lighting on the porch and stairs, contrast tape on step edges, a second handrail, night lights; no driving until vision meets the state standard. Guideline: Cataract in the Adult Eye Preferred Practice Pattern (2021); Falls Prevention in Community-Dwelling Older Adults: Interventions (2024) [S]

Low back pain: lumbar X-ray at intake to look for a retained fragment at the old wound (and to clear any later MRI); reassurance and staying active; physical therapy with exercise and motor control training, then a home program, with heat; no opioids, no muscle relaxants; a short course of an oral anti-inflammatory only if exercise is not enough. Guideline: Noninvasive Treatments for Acute, Subacute, and Chronic Low Back Pain: A Clinical Practice Guideline From the American College of Physicians (2017) [S]

Goiter: TSH and free T4; thyroid ultrasound with the sonographic pattern of each nodule; fine-needle aspiration only for a nodule that meets size and pattern thresholds; follow-up ultrasound at an interval set by the findings; return for trouble swallowing or breathing, voice change or rapid growth. Guideline: 2015 American Thyroid Association Management Guidelines for Adult Patients with Thyroid Nodules and Differentiated Thyroid Cancer (2015) [S]

Knees: quadriceps strengthening, walking and tai chi; topical diclofenac; a stick in the outside hand on slopes. Guideline: 2019 American College of Rheumatology/Arthritis Foundation Guideline for the Management of Osteoarthritis of the Hand, Hip, and Knee (2019); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, cataract and rheumatoid arthritis/osteoarthritis monographs (2026) [S]

Instructions by ear: every plan explained aloud with teach-back, medicine schedules recorded as voice reminders and shown by demonstration, and large-print copies for his household. Guideline: Cataract in the Adult Eye Preferred Practice Pattern (2021) [S]
Referral to ophthalmology (cataract), Ines Delacroix-Moreno, MD, ordered 2026-04-07 [S]
